title: Retry-topic and dead-letter topic names are not specified
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Error Handling and Resilience Standard v3.docx
description: Version 3 has no Kafka retry or dead-letter rule, and Arch v5 describes the ladder as the retry topics at 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and then the .dlt topic. No source in this WP gives the topic names, partitions or the exact suffix set of the retry topics and the .dlt topic for rwb.<short>.events.v1, so the standard states the ladder and the owner and leaves the names open.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 ('Retry topics 1 min / 10 min / 1 h, then .dlt + alert') and slide 22 ('Failures go to retry topics (1 min, 10 min, 1 h) and then to the dead-letter topic'); Template and Rules v1 §R4 ('topic rwb.<short>.events.v1, with retry and .dlt topics'); no naming rule for retry or .dlt topics in the WP sources
proposed: Name the topics rwb.<short>.events.v1.retry.1m, rwb.<short>.events.v1.retry.10m, rwb.<short>.events.v1.retry.1h and rwb.<short>.events.v1.dlt in the naming library (RWB-PLT-E1047) and the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog, and cite them from section 8.3 of this standard.

title: Outbox scope: Epics 1 and 2 in version 3, every service in Arch v5
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Error Handling and Resilience Standard v3.docx
description: Version 3 keeps the outbox for outbound work in Epics 1 and 2 and for the reference workflow when Temporal is unavailable. Arch v5 gives every service a transactional outbox and an inbox in its own schema. The two statements are kept in version 4, with the Arch v5 reading recorded as the target scope and the Epic 1 and Epic 2 wording as the as-built position.
evidence: Version 3 A31 ('The outbox stays for outbound work in Epics 1 and 2') and A36 ('The reference workflow in E2-043 writes through the outbox'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 ('every service: own schema with outbox and inbox') and slide 22 (outbox relay, inbox processed_event); ADR-015 and DP-09
proposed: Read the outbox and inbox rule as applying to all 19 services for the target and keep the Epic 1 and Epic 2 sentences as the as-built position, with the R-PREC precedence rule (Arch v5 first) recorded in the Change Register.

title: No message ID for a REST hop timeout or a dead-lettered event
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Error Handling and Resilience Standard v3.docx
description: The standard adds no message ID and the error and message standard has no code for a REST hop timeout or for an event parked on a .dlt topic. Version 4 states the RFC 9457 problem detail for the REST timeout and the alert path for the dead letter instead of inventing a code; whether the message standard will add MSG-GEN codes for these two failures is open.
evidence: Version 3 A43 ('These are the only messages used for the Temporal and Drools failures in this standard. No message ID is added by this standard'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 ('Errors: RFC 9457 problem details', REST column)
proposed: Keep RFC 9457 problem details for a REST hop timeout and the alert path for a .dlt event in this standard, and decide in the error and message standard whether two new MSG-GEN codes are needed.

title: Role that replays a dead-lettered event is not named
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Error Handling and Resilience Standard v3.docx
description: Arch v5 gives the dead-letter topic an alert and a replay tool but names no role. Version 3 gives the platform administrator the outbound queue and the workflow failures. Version 4 records the platform administrator as the alert and replay role and leaves the split between the platform and the owning service open.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 22 ('then to the dead-letter topic with an alert and a replay tool'); Version 3 A24 (Workflow and Workflow failed rows: 'Platform administrator'); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (platform team runs the stuck-workflow scan, JOB-21)
proposed: Record the platform administrator as the role that receives the .dlt alert and runs the replay tool, with the owning service fixing the cause; put the split in the observability and monitoring design.

title: The 2 s REST timeout equals the 2 s screen target
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Error Handling and Resilience Standard v3.docx
description: Arch v5 gives a 2 s timeout to each REST hop and a 2 s p95 target to the whole screen, planned at about 1.2 s. A hop that runs to its ceiling therefore uses the whole screen budget, and the sources do not say whether the 2 s is a per-call ceiling or the end-to-end budget.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 ('Timeouts 2 s, circuit breaker per downstream, GET retry once with jitter' and 'total about 1.2 s against the 2 s target'); slide 11 ('Timeout, retry: 2 s; retry GET only'); NFR screen response < 2 s (p95)
proposed: Read the 2 s as the per-call ceiling and 1.2 s as the planning figure for the composed screen; record both figures in the availability, performance and recovery design and in the NFR harness.
